_note: Lightweight tier. Trigger cases mirror how the limit-wrapup hook directive and Rahul actually phrase it; near-misses guard against 'wrap' collisions and normal git flow.

evals.prompt:
[limit-wrapup] Account usage warning (this fires at most once per threshold per session):
- 5h window: 87% of usage budget consumed, resets 18:00 (2h); recent burn ~14%/h across all sessions -> ~0.9h of headroom at this rate
If the remaining work on the current task likely exceeds the remaining budget, wrap up cleanly soon (finish the current atomic step, commit WIP, write a brief handoff). If it comfortably fits, continue and ignore this. [Context: mid-way through a large multi-file refactor with ~2h of work remaining]
expected_behavior: Finishes only the current atomic step; starts no new work after the warning
Creates or reuses a wip/<date>-<slug> branch (never commits the WIP to main/master)
Writes HANDOFF.md containing: state of work, ordered next steps, and an exact resume command
HANDOFF.md is included in the WIP commit
Final message is a brief summary + resume pointer, then stops (no further task work)

Running low on weekly budget (91% used). Wrap up: commit whatever is in progress and leave me a handoff so tomorrow's session can resume.
Wrap this function in a try/catch and add a retry.
Commit my changes to a new branch and push it up.
